thread:
Micah: FYI Hyperlane reported a spike of 429s from their Dedicated pool during yesterday's morning peak. They say burst credits were available but requests got throttled. @Anya @Dorian for visibility.

Anya: Looking into it. Can you paste the request ids and exact time window? Any auth errors observed?

Micah: They reported 2025-09-15 09:21-09:28 UTC. Example log they provided:

Micah: ```
{"ts":"2025-09-15T09:22:10Z","req_id":"hl-req-4739","status":429,"reason":"admission_reject","policy":"token_tps","detail":"burst_credits=0, available_headroom=0"}
```

Anya: I pulled their Dedicated config: pool=ded-az1-hl, commit=1500 tps, burst_ceiling=2500 tps, headroom_policy=static-5pct. Autoscaler logs show no scale actions in that window. @autoscale-bot any telemetry?

autoscale-bot: No scale-up triggered. Observed short latency spikes and 95th pct GPU util ~68%. Admission control started rejecting when token rate exceeded burst_ceiling.

Dorian: Could be a mismatch between billing/burst ledger and runtime token bucket. @Leila, can you check the burst credits ledger ingestion around 09:00-09:15?

Leila: Checking ledger now. At 09:00 ledger shows ~120k burst tokens remaining. However, one billing collector had an ingestion lag of ~2h; runtime uses a local credit cache refreshed every 5m. I see evidence: per-tenant credit cache was reset at 09:08 due to an auth service refresh and reloaded stale credits (0) then reconciled at 09:12.

Micah: Customer saw 429s 09:08-09:12 exactly. They say they were actively sending requests but had no auth downtime. We forwarded their request ids and timeline.

Anya: Repro hypothesis: if auth cache refresh happens while sustained burst >commit, runtime admission does a local check and sees 0 burst credits during cache miss → rejects. Queueing should smooth this but static headroom + burst_ceiling logic causes hard rejects when threshold exceeded.

Dorian: Steps I used to repro locally: rotate tenant auth token (force cache reload) and replay a sustained 2.6k tps load for ~2m. Admission rejects spike during the cache-miss window.

Dorian: Proto log snippet from a local run:
```
[09:08:05] cache: tenant/hyperlane refreshed (old_ts=169, new_ts=0)
[09:08:06] admission: token_bucket_lookup -> cache_miss -> credits=0 -> reject
[09:08:30] billing-reconcile: push credits -> credits=123456 -> accept
```

Leila: Root cause summary: billing ingestion lag + auth/cache refresh created a brief window where runtime saw zero credits. Billing ledger actually had credits but runtime cache was stale.

Micah: Immediate mitigation for the customer: 1) lower their burst_ceiling to reduce sudden admission rejects (temporary), 2) advise retry/backoff on client, 3) we opened an internal ticket to fix reconciliation gaps. Sent initial customer note.

Dorian: Proposed fix: on cache-miss treat as 'defer to remote lookup' or use last_known_credits with short grace window (eg last_good_ts < 60s) instead of zero. Also add a background reconciliation hook that pushes current credits to runtime on surge detection. I'll draft RFC.

Leila: Operational fixes: surface billing ingestion lag metric on Console, add alert when collector lag >10m, and implement an atomic reconcile endpoint to push credits to runtime for affected tenants.

Anya: Also check admission control logic: when headroom_policy=static-5pct we should prefer queueing over hard rejects for short spikes. Might add a soft-fail path that allows short token bursts while remote lookup pending.

Dorian: Will open a PR for the cache-miss fallback today; target canary tonight 02:00 UTC with 1% traffic.

eng-oncall: Plan approved for canary. Monitor realtime 429 rate, admission rejects, and collector lag during rollout. If anything looks off, rollback immediately.

Micah: Drafted the customer follow-up: explain root cause (auth cache + billing ingestion mismatch), mitigation steps, and proposed timeline for fix. Will update Hyperlane after canary. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
